packages.summary:
Saving is now reliable, a finished compute is committed in one transaction, and the saved mosaic is checked against its palette.

Save path in useProject:
- Every edit raises a per-part generation counter (rec, mosaic, progress, image). A save writes all unsaved parts in ONE readwrite transaction through the new db.saveProjectState. The mosaic is always written together with its progress.
- Debounce is 250 / 150 / 300 ms, with a maximum wait of 2 s.
- beforeunload, pagehide and visibilitychange(hidden) write immediately without a prior read and call commit(). Edits now survive a reload or a closed tab 50 ms later.
- Failed parts stay dirty and are written again with the next edit, or automatically after 2 / 5 / 15 / 60 s. No unhandled rejections.
- The hook exposes saveState, saveError, retrySave() (never rejects), exportCurrent() (in-memory backup via the new projects.buildProjectExport), integrityError, manualEdits (meta.manualEdits, counted in touchMosaic and reset by compute) and createBackupCopy(suffix) (flush, then duplicateProject).

compute():
- The snapshot is used only to build the worker inputs. computedWith is the key of the snapshot; in custom mode it uses the result palette.
- New mosaicRev = uid() and computedImageRev = r.imageRev.
- db.commitComputed reads the LATEST stored record inside the transaction, merges only the compute-owned fields and writes record, mosaic (with rev) and progress together. If the record is gone it rejects 'deleted' and writes nothing.
- The in-memory merge goes into the latest record, so a rename or joint change made during the compute is kept and shows as stale. Pending mosaic and progress saves of the replaced grid are discarded.

Other parts:
- integrity.ts: maxColorIndex and checkMosaicIntegrity. The loader (restoreComputed) shows a stored grid only if the revisions match and every colour index is inside the palette.
- Image identity: setPhoto sets imageRev. computeKey adds `im`, and the key of legacy projects stays byte-identical.
- db.ts: commit() after the last request; a closed connection is reopened and the transaction retried once; new txMulti helper.
- deleteProject, duplicateProject, importProject and createProject each run as one transaction.
- ImageBitmaps are closed when replaced or unmounted.
packages.notes:
Deviations from the steps:
- Save model: instead of per-key {t, fn} timers plus a failedKeys set, I track a generation counter per part (rec, mosaic, progress, image) and write ALL unsaved parts in one transaction. This is a strict superset of the step:
  - flush() and the timer run the same code.
  - mosaic+progress, and palette+mosaic after a colour removal, are always written atomically.
  - Failed keys are retried with the next edit and by the backoff.
- flush() rejects on failure, so createBackupCopy aborts if the original cannot be saved. retrySave() resolves true/false and never rejects, so wave 2 can use it directly as onClick.
- Normal saves are guarded: the transaction reads the stored record first.
  - If the record is missing (deleted elsewhere), nothing is written and saveError.code becomes 'deleted'.
  - If stored.mosaicRev differs (computed elsewhere), only the user's record edits are merged over the stored compute fields (keepStoredComputeFields). The outdated mosaic/progress is not written, and the hook takes over the stored result.
- Page-leave events (beforeunload, pagehide, visibilitychange hidden) write without reading first and call commit(). The audit measured that only writes issued immediately survive unload. In-memory flags still prevent resurrecting deleted projects or writing stale grids.
- Results from other tabs: commitComputed and deleteProject emit events in the same page plus over BroadcastChannel('mosaicplan').
  - A reopened Workspace or another tab adopts a foreign compute without a reload. It takes the full stored record if it has no unsaved edits; otherwise it keeps its own edits.
  - This covers "leave during compute, reopen" without the wave-3 job registry. The reopened view still shows no computing indicator until the result arrives; that is the job registry (w3-live-preview).
- If commitComputed fails for a reason other than 'deleted' (e.g. quota), the result stays in memory, saveError is set, and the next save writes record+mosaic+progress together (guard 'exists'). No misleading "compute failed" message appears.
- saveError.code has the extra value 'deleted' besides quota/connection/other. Wave-2 banners should map unknown codes to the generic text.
- ProjectRecord.meta is now typed ProjectRecordMeta = ProjectMeta & {manualEdits?}, defined in db.ts, so core/types.ts (owned by w1-cut-correctness) is untouched.
- serialize.ts: StoredMosaic.rev is optional and survives pack/unpack, but only when it is set (deep-equal tests unchanged). unpackMosaic returns MosaicDataWithRev.
- Loader:
  - computed=null plus integrityError='mismatch' covers four cases: rev/index failure, missing mosaic for a record that claims computedWith, unparsable layout, and wrong array lengths.
  - I also set computeError='integrity', so wave 1 shows the message (new i18n key compute.err.integrity, de/en/tr) under the compute button without editing StepCompute.tsx. compute() clears it; an adoption that passes clears it too.
  - Wave 2 may drop this once its banner exists.
  - compute.err.deleted is also new.
- No files outside ownership were edited (outOfOwnershipEdits empty). These were not done because the files are owned elsewhere: Home.tsx bitmap close() (w2-design-system), StepPdf object-URL revoke (w5), Projects.tsx try/catch (w2-android-platform).
- Known side effect: closing the bitmap on unmount means a PDF generation still running after the user leaves the Workspace now fails at api.originalPreview (closed bitmap → caught error) instead of finishing in the background. StepPdf (w5) should take originalPreview before its first await.
- Baseline check: my e2e failed 17/19 against a build of the previous persistence code, so the checks really catch the bugs. Caveat: port 4301 turned out to be occupied by another agent's preview server, so that run hit their build. That build includes unmodified persistence code.
- e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README were not changed. Preview server stopped. The node_modules symlink is not committed (gitignored).

packages.summary: Every planned cut piece now meets the user's minimum width. pieceCuttable only got stricter: the old 2A/P >= min/2 rule stays, and the piece must also pass minCaliperWidth >= min - 1e-6, with an explicit check for empty pieces. The new geometry helpers are convexHull, minCaliperWidth, minInteriorAngle, distToBoundary and pointStrictlyInside. Triangle edits are now checked like line edits: 'diag-empty' when the joint is wider than the tile, 'too-small' below the minimum. SUB edits use the same subdivisionCuttable rule as compute. Choosing the shape a cell already has (same kind and parameters) changes nothing and keeps its progress. New exports: checkCellKind, sameCellKind, allowedCellKinds and repairDegenerateCells (for wave 2 to call on load). analyzeCut returns finite zeros with invalid:true for empty pieces instead of ±Infinity. subRects returns empty pieces instead of flipped negative rectangles when the joint is too wide. For non-convex stones, cut lines are split at the stone's edges. Through cuts come first; notch cuts (cutKinds 'notch') end at the inner corner and start at the raw-tile border or at the last through cut. Placement prefers the fewest notches. Convex output is byte-identical to the old code (checked on rect, triangle, hexagon and 3,000 random pieces). In the stone dialog: notch cuts have their own wording ('Einschnitt i: von … bis Innenecke …', or 'bis zur Steinkante' when the end is not a corner), invalid pieces get a 'cut.invalid' message, convex cut pieces show their narrowest point in mm, and old pieces below the minimum get a warning badge. The Dreiecke, 2×2, 3×3 and Kantenschnitt-Apply buttons are disabled with the reason as tooltip, and the reasons are also listed below the buttons for touch users. Cut template: notch cuts are dotted orange with an inner-corner marker, edge labels sit outside the edge on its normal, the raw-tile size moved into a caption under the template, and a 'schwierig zu schneiden' badge appears below 25° (display only). DEFAULT_SHAPES.minPieceMm is now 2. The setting is relabelled 'Schmalste Stelle eines Schnittteils (mm)' and has a hint. The StepShapes hints for subdivision and triangles use the same check as compute. All new text is in de, en and tr.
packages.notes:
Verification: npm run typecheck, npm test (93 tests, including 39 new ones in tests/w1-cut-correctness.test.ts) and npm run build all pass. Against vite preview on port 4301: e2e/run-e2e.cjs passes 17/17 and e2e/w1-cut-correctness.e2e.cjs passes 22/22. Screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/wave1/w1-cut-correctness/e2e and …/e2e-own; I reviewed them. The preview server is stopped.

Decisions and deviations:
1) analyzeCut on an invalid piece returns yieldPerRaw 1, as the package step says, not 0. Stats therefore count one raw tile per invalid piece as an upper bound, and also count it under notFitting and as shape 'custom' with size 0×0. stats.ts belongs to w1-material-quantities: an invalidPieces counter or skipping these pieces is up to them.
2) cutKinds is a required field on CutInfo; analyzeCut is the only producer. If another package builds CutInfo literals (for example in tests), the merge will need cutKinds: [] added there.
3) For non-convex stones I added one step beyond the plan. Notch cuts are clipped to the area left after the through cuts, so a notch starts at the previous through cut instead of at the raw-tile border (example: 'Einschnitt von (6|2) bis Innenecke (3|2)').
4) subRects now clamps sub-tile size to ≥ 0. Before, a joint wider than the tile could make flipped negative rectangles pass the size check (for example a 2 mm tile, 3 mm joint, 3×3 at min ≤ 1.33). Only invalid input is affected.
5) repairDegenerateCells also repairs SUB cells and LINE or SUB cells whose stored parameters are missing. The colour kept is that of the first piece (c1 for DIAG/LINE, sub[0] for SUB). Cells that are only below the minimum are not changed.
6) setCellKind now returns the type CellKindError | null, which is still compatible with the old string | null. allowedCellKinds has an unused _data parameter to match the specified signature.

i18n overrides in my ext file (no other ext file overrides these keys): shapes.minPiece, edit.err.too-small, cut.nonConvex, pdf.nonConvex, stone.templateLegend, free.thin. The free.thin change is wording only and says the check is approximate for non-convex pieces; freeform validation logic is unchanged, but it now warns more often because pieceCuttable is stricter. New keys: shapes.minPieceHint, shapes.subTooSmallW, shapes.diagTooSmall, edit.err.diag-empty, edit.notPossible, edit.diag, cut.invalid, cut.notch, cut.notchEdge, cut.difficult, stone.invalid, stone.minWidth, stone.belowMin. The old key shapes.subTooSmall is now unused.

Follow-ups for other packages:
(a) pdf.ts (not owned in wave 1) still prints every cutLine as 'Schnitt i' in red. The coordinates are correct and no line crosses the stone, and pdf.nonConvex now says not to snap cuts that end at an inner corner. The PDF owner should use cutKinds to label notches separately (cut.notch) and skip info.invalid pieces.
(b) The golden mosaic hashes will change, because both the stricter rule and the new default of 2 mm change automatic cut choices. Measured on the samples at min 2: fewer split cells, more 2×2 cells in portrait, no pieces under the minimum, mean ΔE change within ±0.2.
(c) FreeformEditor (wave 3): the modal grows with each new point row and moves the drawing area under the cursor, so clicks can miss. The e2e works around this by re-reading the SVG position before each click.
(d) Wave 2 should call repairDegenerateCells on load.
(e) Optional for the next mosaic.ts owner: the line-cut search could skip offsets that cannot meet the minimum width (performance only; skeptics advised against it).

No edits outside my owned files; all other files are new and unique to this package. The node_modules symlink and dist are git-ignored and not committed.

packages.summary:
Analysis step now runs about 4–5× faster with bit-identical output. Golden hashes were recorded before any code change and are unchanged afterwards. Hot-loop changes in computeMosaic: the whole-cell statistics are now a plain sum loop instead of groupOf(() => 0, 1), and the line search uses integer group counts. At 1.25M cells, analyze went from 8.6 s to 1.8 s (21 %) and with shapes off from 4.9 s to 1.1 s (23 %).

Custom palette mode ('custom') now keeps every colour across a compute: input order, hex, name and material, including unused colours with 0 stones. FixedColor.code was added: codes are kept when they are unique positive integers, otherwise numbered 1…n. All other modes behave exactly as before.

New file src/core/paletteOps.ts adds piecesPerColor, planColorRemoval and planMaterialMerge / applyMaterialMerge / mergePaletteFromMaterials. The merge appends missing materials and removes colours that have no material through removePaletteColor in descending index order, so existing indices and codes stay valid.

StepColors changes:
- 'Palette aus Materialien' after a compute merges instead of replacing. A confirmation dialog first shows the stones that will move, the max ΔE, the list of removed colours (with target colour, stones and ΔE), the added colours, and the colours linked or recoloured; afterwards a notice repeats the numbers.
- Without a compute, the palette is still replaced, but there is now a confirmation when existing colours would be discarded.
- Removing a colour opens a dialog with the stone count and a replacement-colour selector, sorted by ΔE with the nearest suggested.
- Rows with 0 stones are muted and tagged 'nicht verwendet'; the header shows 'x von y verwendet'.
- New texts are in de/en/tr in src/i18n/ext/w1-mosaic-core.ts.
packages.notes:
1. Known limit until wave 2: useProject.ts:295 (owned by w1-persistence) still drops p.code when it builds the custom fixedPalette. Until wave 2 passes `code: p.code`, a recompute renumbers custom codes to 1..n in input order. This is identical for palettes without gaps. After a colour is deleted (e.g. 1,2,3,5) a recompute renumbers it to 1,2,3,4. That is still better than before (no deletion, no L* reordering). The custom-mode hint text only promises order and unused colours, not codes, so it stays true both before and after wave 2.

2. Optional monomorphic groupOf (Int8Array labels): I implemented and measured it. The hashes were identical, but there was no measurable gain on a search-heavy config (city sample, detail 0.9, 74k cells: 534–604 ms either way), so I reverted it to keep the diff minimal. The line-search buffer reuse (part c) was not done, as the skeptic advised.

3. Deviations and additions to the plan:
- Merge targets are the exact minimum-ΔE kept colour (all kept candidates are compared). They are passed explicitly as the replacement argument to removePaletteColor, so a removed colour never takes a two-hop path via another colour that is about to be removed. Targets can include newly appended materials; in the test, Haut hell goes to the new Rosa.
- Linked palette entries whose material hex has changed take over the material hex. Stones keep their index; the dialog reports this as 'recolored' with the stone count and ΔE.
- A material whose hex exactly matches a kept palette colour is not appended twice.
- When nothing is computed and the palette is not empty, the replace path now asks for confirmation before discarding the existing colours. An empty palette is still replaced immediately.
- Both dialogs snapshot palette, data and api.version. If anything changed before the user confirms, nothing is applied and a 'Palette wurde inzwischen geändert' notice is shown.
- planColorRemoval sorts candidates by exact ΔE (deltaE(formula, …)). The nearest one is preselected and always passed explicitly.

4. Fixtures and tests:
- tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json follows the agreed format (samples plus modes). To regenerate: UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npx vitest run tests/w1-mosaic-core.test.ts.
- tests/golden/w1-mosaic-core-custom-reference.json holds old-implementation per-hex counts. It was made once by a scratch script against the original code and must not be regenerated.
- tests/w1-mosaic-core.fixtures.ts copies the Home SAMPLES on purpose, so preset edits do not break the golden hashes.

5. Issues found for other owners (I did not change them):
- stats.ts (w1-material-quantities): rawWithReserve/raw for a 0-piece colour is Math.ceil(0 - 1e-9) = -0, which prints as '-0'. My table guards it with Math.max(0, …). The PDF legend (pdf.ts:333) can still print -0 for unused custom colours, which are now kept.
- pdf.ts: the main legend lists every palette entry, so unused custom colours appear there with 0 stones. A later PDF package should mark them 'nicht verwendet' or filter them, like the material list already does.
- color.ts describeColor names #A02432 (crimson) 'Orange' and #FFFF00 'Hellgelbgrün'. The naming looks off, but it is outside this package.
- README limitation 'getestet bis 2 Mio.' and the timings belong to w7-docs-e2e.

6. Bench details: an old/new comparison script and copies of the original code are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/wave1/w1-mosaic-core/scripts/bench.ts (with orig/mosaic.orig.ts). E2E screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/wave1/w1-mosaic-core/e2e-own and …/e2e.

7. The preview server was stopped. The node_modules symlink is gitignored and not committed. No dependencies were added.

packages.summary: I rewrote the material-quantity core in src/core/stats.ts. Raw tiles are now counted per colour and per group of identical cut shapes: raw = Σ ⌈n/yield⌉ per group. Shapes count as identical under 0/90/180/270° rotation, but not when mirrored, because glass has a face side. Before, the code added up 1/yield across all shapes and rounded once, so the count could be too low. The group key is built from polyInRaw, rounded to 0.1 mm and moved to its bounding-box origin. It also ignores which vertex comes first and the winding direction, and it is cached in a WeakMap. Only pieces with yield > 1 go into the per-colour Map<CutInfo,count>. Whole tiles and pieces that do not fit are counted directly, so there is no extra cost for them. rawExact stays as the lower bound. rawWithReserve = ⌈raw·(1+r)⌉, using a helper that is safe against floating-point errors. A NaN or negative reserve counts as 0. rawArea = Σ raw·rawW·rawH, so waste in m² and % now matches the raw-tile count shown. New field Stats.perMaterial lists each material with: materialId (null for the 'ohne Material' group), material, colors, rawW, rawH, pieces, raw, need, stock, toBuy, packs, packsToBuy and cost. need = Σ rawWithReserve of the linked colours. A stock of 0 counts as recorded. Packs need piecesPerPack > 0 and cost needs price > 0; otherwise both stay empty and nothing is estimated. Colours without a material, or whose material is missing, go into one 'ohne Material' group that uses the grid tile size. totalCost now comes from perMaterial, so a material shared by two colours is bought once. costComplete is false when a colour with stones lacks a material, a pack size or a price, and also when there are invalid colour indices. Per colour there are new flags materialMissing and rawAssumedGrid. makeRawSizeFn now returns the same two flags; this is backward compatible. Stats also gets missingMaterials and invalidColorPieces. Pieces with a colour index outside the palette are no longer skipped with `continue`. They are counted in pieces, area, shape and size totals, so their area is no longer counted as joint. They are kept out of the raw and material need. I also updated the hint text under the material calculation in DE/EN/TR (via my src/i18n/ext file) to describe the new counting and to call it a "Richtwert".
packages.notes:
Effect on the four sample projects (old → new raw tiles, reserve 10 %): Porträt 5786→5831 (+0.8 %), Landschaft 11023→11061 (+0.3 %), Tier 5256→5287 (+0.6 %), Stadtbild 18794→18816 (+0.1 %). Waste % rises to match, e.g. Porträt 4.69→5.62 %. That is less than the 2–8 % in the risk note, which was measured against a never-share upper bound. computeStats on 500k cells takes about 750 ms instead of about 630 ms (measured with npx tsx).

Decisions and deviations:
(1) Per-colour cs.packs/cs.cost are kept, because StepPlan and the PDF still show per-colour packs until waves 3/5 (as the risk note says). cs.cost is now only set when there is a price, so it is never shown as 0. The hint text now says that cost is per material and that the 'Pack.' column shows each colour on its own. The per-colour stock warning in StepPlan.tsx:419 (stock > 0, per colour) is not in my files and is still wrong for shared materials. perMaterial.toBuy/packsToBuy are the correct values for wave 5.
(2) Colours whose materialId points to a missing material go into the single 'ohne Material' group (materialId null) with materialMissing=true. Stats.missingMaterials lists every palette index with a dangling ID, even colours with no stones.
(3) invalidColorPieces are part of the geometric totals (pieces, stoneArea, perShape, perSize, placed) but not of perColor, raw or material totals. The invariant is Σ perColor.pieces + invalidColorPieces = pieces. Waste uses only the stone area of valid colours. costComplete is false when invalidColorPieces > 0. Nothing displays invalidColorPieces/missingMaterials/rawAssumedGrid yet; the UI and PDF guards belong to wave 3 (w3-pdf-foundations) and wave 5.
(4) No cut allowance and no change to rectangle yield (pieces.ts belongs to w1-cut-correctness; the skeptic said the default should stay 0). The count is a safe upper bound under the analyzeCut yield model. Strips of different widths in the same colour (e.g. 2.5 + 3.5 mm) are deliberately not packed into one tile (FFD packing is deferred).
(5) New exported helpers for w5-stats-engine: canonicalOutline, rawGroupKey, rawFromSharedCuts, withReserve, packsFor, materialTotals, and the types MaterialStat and RawSize.
(6) README 'Materialbedarf' needs updating in wave 7: per-shape-group rounding, waste based on the rounded count, packs/costs per material.
(7) My e2e script writes one material straight into IndexedDB (mosaicplan/materials) after the first app start, then assigns it to colours 01/02 through the selects in the StepColors palette table. If w1-mosaic-core changes that table's structure, the selector `[data-testid="palette-table"] tbody tr select` may need adjusting.
No edits outside my owned files; the node_modules symlink and dist are not committed.

packages.summary:
Touch taps on the mosaic can no longer leak into the stone dialog they open. On touchend after a recognised finger or pen tap the Viewer calls preventDefault, so no ghost mousedown/mouseup/click reaches the dialog. pointercancel now has its own handler that only resets state. The tap slop is 10 px for touch/pen and 5 px for mouse, and finger/pen presses longer than 500 ms do not count as taps.

Taps at overview zoom no longer hit random stones. If the hit stone is smaller than 28 CSS px on screen, a touch/pen tap does not pick it. The view zooms in around the tap point (220 ms animation) until that stone is about 40 px, capped at 120 px/mm, and a 1.5 s hint 'Zum Antippen hineingezoomt – jetzt den Stein antippen' appears. Mouse behaviour is unchanged.

Each Modal now has its own history entry (new module src/ui/modalHistory.ts):
- Back, popstate or page.goBack() closes the topmost dialog first, nested dialogs last-in-first-out, and the URL stays the same.
- ✕, Esc and the backdrop go back through history.
- Closing from code (Save/Cancel) removes the dialog's own entry.
- The StrictMode double mount creates no duplicate entry (checked in the dev server).
- Esc only closes the topmost dialog.
- The backdrop closes only when both pointerdown and pointerup happened on it.

parseLocaleNum (src/ui/numberParse.ts) reads numbers per language: de/tr '1.000' → 1000 and '1.000,5' → 1000.5, en '1,000' → 1000. '0.125' stays 0.125. Spaces are accepted only as thousands grouping in groups of three. Unclear input ('1,2,3', '12abc', '12 5') gives NaN, so nothing is committed. NumberInput uses it in both places and shows an inline hint '→ 1000 cm' when grouping or spaces were removed. The preview hint and the laying-mode hint were reworded in de/en/tr to describe the new tap behaviour.
packages.notes:
Choices that differ from or add to the steps:

1. The 500 ms long-press limit applies only to touch/pen; mouse stays exactly as before, matching the skeptic's corrected proposal ('Mouse behaviour stays as it is'). The size gate uses the hit piece's bounding box (min side × scale), as the step says, so thin edge strips and 2×2/3×3 sub-stones also zoom in before they can be picked. Zooming stops if the scale is already at maxS (120 px/mm), so a stone can never become impossible to pick.

2. tapHandled is a component ref, and its touchend listener (non-passive) is registered in its own effect with no dependencies. So the flag survives even if the pointer-listener effect is rebuilt between pointerup and touchend. Pan and pinch are unaffected because the flag is set only for recognised taps (verified in e2e). On a tap the Viewer blurs a focused input, because the cancelled mouse events no longer move focus. The canvas carries data-scale for tests; the fit, zoom-in and zoom-out buttons have data-testids.

3. The modal history lives in a separate testable module, src/ui/modalHistory.ts. It uses a depth model (state.mpModalDepth) rather than per-id entries, which handles nested dialogs, StrictMode remounts, closing a lower dialog, stale forward entries, reload while on a dialog entry, and a foreign base history.state (kept by spreading).
   - ✕/Esc/backdrop call history.back(), and the dialog closes on the popstate. There is an 800 ms fallback that closes it directly if no popstate arrives.
   - Pure tap rules are in src/ui/project/touchTap.ts.
   - Both of these modules are new files that were not in the planned newFiles list.

4. parseNum(s, lang='de') is still exported from components.tsx but now delegates to parseLocaleNum; nothing else in the codebase uses it. Spaces are stricter than 'strip all': they are accepted only as thousands grouping in groups of three, so '12 5' is NaN instead of silently becoming 125.

5. The '→ 1000 cm' hint is inline after the unit. An absolutely positioned version covered the label of the next field.

6. My i18n ext file also overrides preview.hint and plan.layModeHint in de/en/tr, so the UI honestly says that a finger tap on stones that are too small only zooms in and that long presses don't count. No other ext file overrides these keys.

7. Not done here, for later packages:
   - Android APK: the back button only closes dialogs once the planned @capacitor/app backButton listener calls history.back() when canGoBack is true. My history entries make canGoBack true while a dialog is open. main.tsx and package.json are outside my ownership, and @capacitor/app is not added.
   - Workspace steps still use replaceState (outside ownership).
   - Not done: undo, the haptic feedback (deferred in the plan), opening the stone dialog on a long press in laying mode, and a 16px input font-size for iOS Safari.
   - README (owned by w7) should mention the tap-to-zoom behaviour and the back-closes-dialog behaviour.

8. e2e/run-e2e.cjs was not modified and still passes unchanged.

packages.summary:
The materials CSV import and export now work reliably with German Excel. The CSV code moved out of the UI into the pure module src/core/materialsCsv.ts, which has no UI or i18n imports.

Import:
- Strips the BOM and honours a `sep=X` line. Otherwise it picks the delimiter once from the header, counting only outside quotes, in the order `;`, tab, `,`, and splits only on that character.
- Decodes the encoding German Excel actually writes: UTF-8 with or without BOM, Windows-1252 (ANSI), Windows-1254 (Turkish ANSI), and UTF-16 ("Unicode-Text", tab-separated).
- Matches column names in de, en and tr without regard to case, umlauts or Turkish letters. When two columns map to the same field, the more specific name wins (for example "Farbnummer" over "Code").
- Converts length columns marked "(cm)" to mm. Columns in m or inch are ignored and reported, never guessed.
- Maps type words: Glas, Keramik, Smalten, Naturstein, cam, seramik. Unknown words become "Sonstiges" with a warning.
- Never guesses numbers. "12,50" becomes 12.5 and "9,5" becomes 9.5. "1.250,50 €" becomes 1250.5. "1.250" in an integer field, or an ambiguous value in a decimal field, is not imported and gets a warning.
- Every skipped or questionable row is reported with its line number and reason, for example an invalid HEX value, more values than header columns, an unclosed quote, a duplicate within the file, or a match against several existing materials.
- A file without a HEX column stops with the error 'Spalte „HEX“ fehlt' instead of reporting "0 importiert".

Export:
- Adds an 'id' column and localized headers.
- Uses `;` with decimal comma for de/tr and `,` with decimal point for en, keeps the BOM, and quotes fields that contain the delimiter, a quote, CR/LF or leading/trailing spaces.
- Export followed by import is lossless in de, en and tr. A "Vorlage herunterladen" button writes the header plus one row clearly marked as an example.

Import preview dialog:
- Shows 'N neu · M aktualisiert · K identisch · F fehlerhaft (Zeile 3: …) · Hinweise: W', with the file's delimiter and encoding, recognised, ignored and missing columns, and lists of failed rows, warnings, updates (field: old → new), new rows and identical rows.

Decisions and deviations from the briefing:
1. The return shape differs a little from the briefing. parseMaterialsCsv(text) only parses and returns {rows, skipped, warnings, columns, ...}, or an error with code 'empty', 'no-header', 'no-hex-column' or 'no-rows'. planMaterialImport(parsed, existing, mode, newId) matches against existing materials and returns {items:[{line, material}], updates:[{line, before, after, changed}], identical, skipped, warnings}. Parsing does not need the material DB; matching does.
2. A present but empty cell counts as the file's value. This lets the user clear a field via CSV, and the preview shows each change before confirming. An invalid cell never overwrites an existing value.
3. Size 0 or empty is imported with a 'size-unknown' warning instead of skipping the row. 0 is the app's existing "unknown" value (raw size falls back to the grid size). Warnings are listed only for rows that will actually be written.
4. If a key matches several existing materials, the row is skipped as 'ambiguous-match' in update mode and never assigned to the "nearest" one. It can still be imported with "Als neu hinzufügen".
5. Duplicate rows within one file are skipped and point back to the first line.
6. Some aliases are deliberately not mapped because they are ambiguous: "Höhe", "Anzahl", "Nr.", "Preis pro Stück". The app's price field is the price per pack. Unmapped columns appear as "nicht erkannt (ignoriert)".
7. Additions beyond the steps: ANSI/UTF-16 decoding (German Excel's default CSV is Windows-1252, which would garble "Länge"); a combined size column ("10x10x4"); title rows before the header are skipped and reported; a stock column in the table; a filtered count in the search.
8. The no-eyedropper hint does not promise a photo-measuring feature, because that feature does not exist yet (requirement 18).
9. A formatter hook reflowed src/core/materialsCsv.ts on disk (one array item per line). That is formatting only.

reviewFixes:
All 18 wave-1 findings are fixed, and everything is green. The fixes are committed and pushed to `ccr-e3c91906-ceq1vn`. HEAD is `04c4affce0e02747c3752d2d02ebd939029fe486`, and the preview server on 4173 is still running.

**Findings and fixes:**
- **Custom-palette edits during a compute:**
  - `commitComputed` in `src/storage/db.ts` now compares the stored palette with the palette the compute started from.
    - Colours only added, or renamed/re-coloured in place: the user's palette is kept and the project shows "Einstellungen geändert".
    - Colours removed or reordered: the result is discarded with a "palette-changed" message, and the old palette and grid stay.
  - The same rule applies in memory, when another tab's result is adopted, and when saving.
  - New `src/storage/computeLock.ts`: palette editing and the mode switch are locked while any compute for the project runs, in this view, a reopened view or another tab (heartbeat via BroadcastChannel).
- **"Farbe entfernen" white-screen crash:** the remove and merge dialogs only render while their snapshot still matches, and close with a notice when the palette or grid changes. New `src/ui/ErrorBoundary.tsx` wraps each view and the whole app.
- **Custom colour numbers renumbered on recompute (two findings):** `useProject.compute` now passes `code`. The e2e now recomputes after removing and after merging and checks the numbers stay.
- **PDF material totals that didn't add up (two findings):** the per-colour table only shows raw tiles. A new "Einkaufsliste je Material" (material shopping list) shows need, stock, to-buy, packs and cost, and its cost total equals the material cost. In the app (step 9, material calculation) the same list shows shortages in red per material, including when stock is 0.
- **PDF notch cuts (two findings):** notches are drawn orange and dotted with a circle at the inner corner. They are numbered as in the stone dialog ("Einschnitt 1 … nicht durchritzen"). Warnings now print before the cut list and are never cut off; the template drawing or font shrinks to make room.

The setting is now "Mindestbreite eines Schnittteils". Hints show the measured values, e.g. "Inkreismaß 1,93 mm < 2 mm (schmalste Stelle 2,33 mm)", and how far the minimum would have to drop for triangles. A new hint says when no edge cut is possible.
